bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / local HarfBuzz history
bug_description.normalized: The saved MSAN crash comes from the harness's second `hb_shape()` call at `test/fuzzing/hb-shape-fuzzer.cc:37`, which shapes a 16-word UTF-32 buffer copied from the last 64 bytes of the exact 100-byte witness. The same witness bytes also back the font blob. `hb_face_create()` accepts that blob as an OpenType font, and AAT positioning later lazy-loads a single `kerx` table whose first subtable is Format1 with attacker-controlled `length = 0x00000010` and `tupleCount = 0x20000000`. In `AAT::KerxSubTableFormat1<...>::driver_context_t::transition()`, the current state-table entry provides the `actions` pointer, while prior `Push` transitions fill the local 8-slot kerning stack to `depth = 8`. The vulnerable bounds check computes `depth * tuple_count` in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic before calling `check_array`; for the witness, `8 * 0x20000000` wraps to `0`, so the guard validates an empty range instead of eight tuples. The immediately following `int v = *actions;` then dereferences that unchecked `FWORD` pointer, and the read faults in `BEInt<short, 2>::operator short()`. The staged `patch.diff` is unrelated, but the local HarfBuzz history contains commit `c8f4cc49272d8bcd47706a6306a625d724349f5a` (`[kerx] Fix integer overflow in multiply`), which fixes this exact testcase by replacing the overflow-prone guard with `check_array2 (actions, depth, tuple_count)`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that stores the raw witness bytes in library state. The blob later backs `hb_face_create()` and every lazy table read, including the crashing `kerx` load.

sink.description: Final crashing read. Dereferencing the unchecked `FWORD *actions` pointer from the prior step executes this big-endian 16-bit load, and MSAN reports the READ fault here.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: SEGV` caused by a READ at `src/hb-machinery.hh:677:10`, with `AAT::KerxSubTableFormat1<AAT::KerxSubTableHeader>::driver_context_t::transition` line 285 immediately above it on the stack.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The only runtime bounds guard multiplies the current kerning-stack depth by attacker-controlled `tupleCount` in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic before validating the `actions` array. For the witness, `depth == 8` and `tuple_count == 0x20000000`, so the product wraps to zero and the guard checks an empty range instead of eight tuples.
root_cause.note: Local HarfBuzz commit `c8f4cc49272d8bcd47706a6306a625d724349f5a` fixes testcase `5754863779053568` by replacing this with `check_array2 (actions, depth, tuple_count)`, which detects the multiplication overflow before scaling.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the attacker-controlled font bytes become the typed `kerx` object used by the vulnerable state machine. Static decoding of the exact witness shows the single sfnt table record points `kerx` to file offset `0x28`, where the first subtable presents Format1 `coverage ... 0x01`, `length = 0x10`, and `tupleCount = 0x20000000`.

utf32_shape_call.note: The saved MSAN stack ends at line 37, so the observed crash occurs during the harness's second `hb_shape()` call on the UTF-32 buffer populated from the last 64 bytes of the same witness.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness stores the exact 100-byte witness as the font blob, copies the last 64 bytes into a 16-word UTF-32 buffer, and the saved MSAN stack shows the crash happens during the second `hb_shape()` call at line 37.
AAT positioning lazy-loads the witness's single `kerx` table. The first subtable reached on the crashing path is Format1 with `length = 0x10` and `tupleCount = 0x20000000`.
Before dispatching the selected subtable, HarfBuzz scopes runtime sanitization to that 16-byte subtable object and enters the Format1 state-machine driver.

Attacker-controlled `Push` transitions fill the local kerning stack to depth 8, the current state-table entry derives `actions`, and the guard `check_array(actions, depth * tuple_count)` overflows its length argument to zero.
The immediately following `*actions` dereference performs a 2-byte big-endian read from the unchecked pointer, and MSAN reports the READ/SEGV at `hb-machinery.hh:677`.

fine_trace.code: hb_blob_t *blob = hb_blob_create ((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Harness step. Passes the raw witness bytes into HarfBuzz's blob constructor; the next step is the first non-harness statement that stores this pointer in library state.
Source. Stores the attacker-controlled byte pointer inside the blob that later backs `hb_face_create()` and every lazy font-table read on the crashing path.

During the saved crash path's second `hb_shape()` call at harness line 37, AAT positioning lazy-loads the admitted `kerx` table from the face and reinterprets its bytes as `AAT::kerx`. Static decoding of the exact witness shows the single sfnt table record points `kerx` to file offset `0x28`; the first subtable reached here has low coverage byte `0x01` (Format1), `length = 0x00000010`, and `tupleCount = 0x20000000`.

Before dispatching the selected subtable, runtime AAT apply-time sanitization is scoped to the current `kerx` subtable object. For this witness that object length is the attacker-controlled `0x10` from step 3, so later `check_array(actions, ...)` is supposed to prove reads stay within a 16-byte subtable window.

fine_trace.code: if (flags & Format1EntryT::Push) { if (likely (depth < ARRAY_LENGTH (stack))) stack[depth++] = buffer->idx; else depth = 0; }
fine_trace.note: The only code that grows the kerning stack is the `Push` arm. On the witnessed chain it must have executed on prior reachable state-machine iterations until the fixed 8-slot stack became full: `ARRAY_LENGTH (stack) == 8`, and with step 3's `tupleCount = 0x20000000` the later multiplication overflows only when `depth == 8`.
Reads the attacker-controlled tuple count from the Format1 subtable header. For the exact witness `table->header.tuple_count()` is `0x20000000`, so `tuple_count` remains `0x20000000`.

fine_trace.code: unsigned int kern_idx = Format1EntryT::kernActionIndex (entry); kern_idx = Types::offsetToIndex (kern_idx, &table->machine, kernAction.arrayZ); const FWORD *actions = &kernAction[kern_idx];
fine_trace.note: Derives the action pointer from attacker-controlled state-table entry data. For extended `kerx` tables `ExtendedTypes::offsetToIndex()` is identity, so the current entry's `kernActionIndex` becomes a direct index into the `kernAction` array and selects the `actions` pointer used by the sink.

Root cause. `check_array()` receives the product `depth * tuple_count` after it has already been computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic. With step 5's `depth == 8` and step 6's `tuple_count == 0x20000000`, the multiplication wraps to `0`, so this guard validates an empty range instead of eight tuples inside the 16-byte subtable object from step 4. Local HarfBuzz commit `c8f4cc49272d8bcd47706a6306a625d724349f5a` fixes testcase `5754863779053568` by replacing this with `check_array2 (actions, depth, tuple_count)`.
Unsafe memory access. After step 8 accepts the wrapped zero-length range, `transition()` immediately dereferences the unchecked `FWORD *actions` pointer and begins consuming kerning data from it.

Sink. Evaluating step 9's `*actions` invokes this big-endian 16-bit load; the saved MSAN trace reports `MemorySanitizer: SEGV` on a READ at `src/hb-machinery.hh:677:10` with step 9 immediately above it on the stack.

poc.trigger: The staged 100-byte witness makes the harness's second `hb_shape()` call at `hb-shape-fuzzer.cc:37` load a `kerx` Format1 subtable with `tupleCount = 0x20000000`. When the state machine reaches an action with kerning-stack depth 8, `check_array (actions, depth * tuple_count)` wraps its length to zero and the subsequent `*actions` read crashes in `BEInt<short, 2>::operator short()`.

format.name: 100-byte synthetic sfnt with a kerx Format1 subtable
format.contract: The staged `poc` is the exact 100-byte witness in `gt_results/arvo_11372/poc`. Its verified trigger semantics are: the sfnt directory contains exactly one table record tagged `kerx` whose offset is `0x00000028`; at that offset the first `kerx` subtable reached by the saved crash path has low coverage byte `0x01` (Format1), `length = 0x00000010`, and `tupleCount = 0x20000000`; and the harness copies the last 64 bytes of the same file verbatim into the 16-word `text32` buffer consumed by the crashing `hb_shape()` call at line 37. On the witnessed chain, HarfBuzz reaches a Format1 action after the kerning stack has filled to depth 8, so the vulnerable guard's length multiplication wraps to zero before `*actions` is read. No broader trigger class beyond this exact overflowed `kerx` Format1 bounds-check chain is claimed.
